body.en: In a Japanese coastal village, the old and respected Hamaguchi, watching from his house on the hill during a harvest festival, feels a long, slow earthquake and then sees the sea draw back far from the shore. From old knowledge he recognises the sign of a tsunami. With no time to warn the villagers celebrating on the beach, he sets fire to his own rice stacks, his whole year's wealth. The villagers rush up the hill to put out the fire, and moments later a giant wave destroys the village below. Hamaguchi's sacrifice saves hundreds of lives, and the grateful people honour him as a *living god*, building a shrine to his spirit while he still lives. Read the prescribed text itself; this guide is in our own words and quotes nothing.

text.en: Exposition
A seaside village celebrates the harvest;
old Hamaguchi watches from the hill.
Rising action
A long, strange earthquake; the sea
pulls back far from the shore.
Climax
He sets fire to his own rice stacks
so the villagers will run up the hill.
Falling action
The people climb to fight the fire
as the giant wave wipes out the village.
Resolution
Realising his sacrifice, they honour him
as a living god with a shrine.

body.en: *Advice to Youth* is a short satirical speech in which Mark Twain pretends to give young people sober moral advice: obey your parents, respect your elders, go to bed early, never handle firearms carelessly, read good books. Each piece of advice is undercut with a comic twist that exposes adult hypocrisy: lying, for example, is not forbidden but should be done skilfully. The deadpan tone, exaggeration and anticlimax make the humour; beneath it lies a serious point about moralising adults and blind obedience.

points.en: A mock-serious speech to the young
Every moral rule has a comic twist

explanation.en: Hearn tells a serious story of sacrifice and wisdom; Twain uses irony to mock moralising.

say.en: Sort each statement.

problem.en: Why is Hamaguchi called a "living god"? Answer in about 100 words.

steps.en: He sacrificed his entire rice harvest, his wealth, without hesitation.
His knowledge and quick thinking saved hundreds of villagers from the tsunami.
The villagers understood his sacrifice and felt deep gratitude.
In their tradition, such a person could be honoured as a god even while alive, and they built a shrine to his spirit.

answer.en: His wise, selfless sacrifice saved the village, and the grateful villagers honoured him as divine during his lifetime.
